question: During a lab meeting on refraction at a boundary between media, which assertion is right?
options: Light always bends away from the normal in denser media.
Refraction changes the frequency of light.
Mirrors refract light into their glass.
Light bends at boundaries according to the refractive indices.
gold_answer: Light bends at boundaries according to the refractive indices.
notes: Team-authored original item on refraction at a boundary between media. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Mirrors refract light into their glass.

claims.text: Total internal reflection occurs beyond the critical angle.

evidence.text: Past the critical angle no refracted ray can satisfy the angle relation, so all light reflects internally.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes complete internal reflection past the angle, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Frequency is set by the source and preserved; only wavelength and speed change in the new medium.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states frequency is preserved, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Speeds were tabulated for light in several media.

claims.verdict_rationale: A tabulation cannot show glass is fastest, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Light always bends away from the normal in denser media.

claims.text: Light slows down when entering an optically denser medium.

evidence.text: The denser medium reduces the wave speed, which is exactly what the higher refractive index records.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states speed falls in denser media, which entails the claim.

claims.text: A straw looks bent because water magnifies it.

evidence.text: The apparent bend comes from direction change at the surface, not from magnification.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage attributes the bend to direction change, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Rainbow sightings were logged against sun and rain geometry.

claims.verdict_rationale: Logging sightings cannot show every shower produces one, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Light bends at boundaries according to the refractive indices.

claims.text: The angles on each side follow the relation between the two indices.

evidence.text: The index-weighted sines of the incidence and refraction angles are equal across the boundary.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the quantitative angle relation, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Reflection and refraction are the same phenomenon.

evidence.text: Reflection returns light to the first medium while refraction transmits it into the second.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage distinguishes the two directions, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Visual acuity was measured with and without corrective lenses.

claims.verdict_rationale: Measuring acuity cannot show all problems are cured, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
